title: Automatic config stabilization: cost-aware revert triggers and reconciliation state machine
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: Config changes to batching, caching or scheduling sometimes improve throughput but can cause transient unit-cost regressions or increased tail latency. Existing rollback signalers trigger too eagerly or lack context about economic trade-offs. We need an automatic stabilization layer that evaluates post-apply health against cost and latency objectives and only reverts when the regression is both materially harmful and cannot be self-healed.
background: We frequently see config flips (batch_size, cache_ttl, kernel-selection heuristics) that pass CI and unit tests but cause increased per-token cost or KV cache thrashing in production traffic patterns. Manual rollbacks are slow; fully automated hard rollbacks are noisy. This ticket proposes a middle-ground: an AutoStabilizer state machine that performs staged verification, cost-impact estimation, synthetic shadow trials, and multi-signal revert decisions with a safety hold period.
design_decisions: 1) Use dual-checkpoint snapshots (pre-apply and post-apply) of routing/config fingerprints and lightweight sample traces rather than full cluster snapshots to keep storage/compute low. 2) Evaluate both economic (cost/unit, tokens/sec) and QoS (p95/p99 latency, error-rate) signals. 3) Combine deterministic guardrails (hard thresholds) with a probabilistic risk score that weights signal severity, customer impact, and traffic skew. 4) Prefer staged soft-rollbacks (traffic split to previous config) before full reversion. 5) Keep the decision logic deterministic and auditable with a generated decision record for each revert action.
acceptance_criteria: 1) AutoStabilizer can be enabled per-tenant and per-route with a config toggle. 2) For any config apply, the system generates pre/post snapshots and runs a 5-minute shadow verification by default. 3) If cost delta > 15% AND p95 latency regresses > 20% sustained over 3 minutes, AutoStabilizer will execute a staged split-back to the previous config within the hold window. 4) All actions write an immutable decision record to the audit log and emit metrics to the Console dashboard. 5) Must include unit tests, integration tests (simulated traffic) and an e2e dry-run mode that exercises the state machine without mutating live traffic.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Implement snapshot schema + lightweight sample trace collector; add config toggle and per-route metadata. Week 2: Implement state machine and risk-scoring service; build decision-record schema; wire up audit log. Week 3: Create staged-split controller (canary traffic split to previous config) + automatic rollback executor. Week 4: Integrate with Console metrics/dashboards and add runbooks and alerting. Week 5: Testing, perf tuning, and gradual rollout to low-traffic tenants.
technical_notes: - Snapshot stored as compressed protobufs of: config-hash, active-kv-cache-keys-metrics, batch-distribution histogram sample, last-1000 request latencies. - Risk score = weighted sum({cost_delta_pct * 0.5, p95_delta_pct * 0.3, error_rate_delta * 0.2}) with a tunable decision threshold. - Use existing rollout infra to implement staged split; leverage runtime routing rules for quick switchback. - Shadow verification uses sampled real traffic in shadow mode with no public response change, and a synthetic traffic generator for low-traffic routes.
monitoring_and_metrics: Emit metrics: autostabilizer.risk_score, autostabilizer.decision_count{result=applied|reverted|soft-split}, autostabilizer.cost_delta_pct, autostabilizer.p95_delta_pct, autostabilizer.action_latency_seconds. Dashboard: per-route timeline with pre/post snapshots, risk score, decision record links. Alerting: page on >=3 full reverts in 1 hour for the same route or a single revert with customer_impact=high.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Dry-run for all tenants (decision records created, no automated action). Phase 2: Enable for internal tenants and staging customers with opt-in; monitor dashboards for 2 weeks. Phase 3: Gradually enable soft-split and then automated staged rollback for P1/P2 routes. Include a global kill-switch and tenant-level opt-out.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for risk scorer and decision logic. - Integration test harness that replays captured traffic traces and asserts expected decisions. - Chaos tests: inject delayed metrics, transient load spikes, and ensure hysteresis prevents flapping. - Performance tests: ensure decision service adds <50ms median latency to apply pipeline.
runbook_and_playbook: Runbook located at https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/AutoStabilizer+Runbook. Playbook contains step-by-step for manual override, forced-revert, re-snapshot, and how to inspect decision records (trace IDs, snapshot IDs, and PR references).
security_and_compliance: Snapshots exclude PII. All decision records and snapshots are encrypted at rest with KMS and access controlled via RBAC. Sensitive fields redacted per compliance policy.
open_questions: 1) Threshold defaults: Should cost_delta threshold be route-specific or globally tuned? 2) How long should the hold window be for short-lived transient regressions? 3) Do we allow ML-based trend prediction (predictive rollback) in phase 1? Recommend no — start deterministic.
